Citation: Kushwaha, S. & Nithiyanandam, Y. The study of heat island and its relation with urbanization in Gurugram, Delhi NCR for the period of 1990 to 2018. ISPRS Archives XLII-5/W3
Methods: LULC classification; LST from thermal band; correlation impervious surface vs LST
Limitations: Single correlation; no spatial statistics; no vegetation effect quantified; no neighbourhood-level priorities
Gap it suggests for my study: No neighbourhood-level (grid/sector) analysis; no control for spatial autocorrelation; no policy prioritisation

Citation: Saurav. Spatial analysis of urban heat island intensity and mitigation strategies using GIS: a case study of Gurugram. Thesis, SPA Bhopal
Spatial unit / scale: Not stated in abstract; appears pixel-level heat-intensity mapping
Methods: Mono-window LST; UTFVI classification; GIS mapping
Key findings (with numbers): UHI formation identified; linked to urban expansion and land-use change (no figures in abstract)
Limitations: Full text unavailable; abstract reports no statistical testing of drivers and no spatial statistics
Gap it suggests for my study: No regression/spatial autocorrelation analysis, no neighbourhood ranking, no GMDA plan link (based on abstract only)

Citation: Malcoti, M.D., Zia, H., Kabre, C., et al. Analysis of urban streets and surface thermal characteristics using thermal imaging camera in residential streets of Gurugram City, India. Environmental Science and Pollution Research 30, 86892-86910
Type: Journal article (peer-reviewed); PhD summary as context
Data: Thermal camera surface temps; air temp loggers (PhD)
Methods: Field thermal imaging; comparison by street geometry, colour, material, shading
Key findings (with numbers): Compact streets 2-4 C cooler; light buildings 1.5-4 C cooler; UHI intensity up to 7.8 C in hottest month (PhD)
Limitations: Few streets; not generalisable city-wide; abstract only (paywall)
Gap it suggests for my study: Street-level effects not scaled city-wide; satellite study can show where they matter; use to interpret results

Citation: Palanisamy, P.A., Zawadzka, J., Jain, K. & Bonafoni, S. Monitoring summer daytime and nighttime decadal trends of land surface temperature over the National Capital Region Delhi. ISPRS Archives XLVIII-1/W2
Data: MODIS MOD11A1 day + night LST (1 km), Google Earth Engine
Methods: Seasonal mean day/night LST; change vs 2000; diurnal range; maps with 2.5 C threshold
Key findings (with numbers): Summer LST rose up to ~10 C (day and night); rural hotter than urban by day, urban hotter by night; lower LST in 2020 linked to COVID lockdown (suggested, not tested)
Limitations: 1 km too coarse for neighbourhoods; no statistical drivers; lockdown link untested; four snapshot years
Gap it suggests for my study: Daytime rural > urban LST in semi-arid NCR: bare land may be hotter than built-up -> must separate bare soil from buildings; Landsat 30 m needed for neighbourhood detail; daytime-only Landsat misses night heat

Citation: Diksha, Kumari, M., Supraja, R.V.K. & Mishra, V.N. Urban heat island assessment using Landsat-derived indices and geographically weighted regression in Sonipat district, India. AIMS Geosciences 12(2), 302-334
Methods: LST, NDVI, NDBI, albedo, sky view factor, solar radiation; UTFVI; Moran's I; OLS then GWR
Limitations: Only two dates, winter season; Landsat 7 gap-filling; no validation; GWR R2 ~0.99 suggests overfitting, no cross-validation; inconsistent reporting
Gap it suggests for my study: Apply same methods with stronger design: pre-monsoon multi-year composites, clear spatial unit, cross-validation, avoid overfitting; first such analysis for Gurugram

Citation: Priyadarshni, P. & Pandey, P. A footprint of UHI in India: a systematic review of causative factors, impacts and mitigation strategies. Frontiers in Sustainable Cities 7
Methods: Systematic search of 4 databases (1,655 records -> 89 studies)
Key findings (with numbers): Core-suburb UHI 2-10 C; ~88% of studies are surface UHI; Delhi most studied (13.33%); drivers: vegetation loss, impervious surfaces, unplanned growth
Limitations: Review only up to 2023; depends on quality of included studies
Gap it suggests for my study: Megacities dominate; calls for smaller cities, field validation, equity analysis, integrated policy -> supports Gurugram + priority areas + policy link

Citation: Rasul, A., Balzter, H., Smith, C., Remedios, J., Adamu, B., Sobrino, J.A., Srivanit, M. & Weng, Q. A review on remote sensing of urban heat and cool islands. Land 6(2), 38
Methods: Narrative review of SUHI/SUCI quantification methods
Key findings (with numbers): Arid/semi-arid cities can show daytime surface cool islands (city cooler than bare surroundings) and night-time heat islands; few studies of LULC-LST in arid/semi-arid climates
Gap it suggests for my study: Explains P04 finding; semi-arid LULC-LST relationship under-studied -> strengthens bare-land gap; choose rural reference carefully

Citation: Zheng, Z., Fong, C.S., Aghamohammadi, N. & Law, Y.K. A systematic review of urban heat island (UHI) impacts and mitigation: health, equity, and policy. Systems 14(1), 82
Key findings (with numbers): Green infrastructure ~1-6 C cooling; cool surfaces ~2-22 C; trees gave more benefit in disadvantaged neighbourhoods; surface and air temperature metrics not interchangeable
Limitations: Small sample; some figures combine unlike comparisons (read critically)
Gap it suggests for my study: Supports spatially differentiated, equity-centred targeting -> priority areas; reminder to keep LST vs air temp distinct

Citation: Weng, Q., Lu, D. & Schubring, J. Estimation of land surface temperature-vegetation abundance relationship for urban heat island studies. Remote Sensing of Environment 89, 467-483
Methods: Spectral mixture analysis (vegetation fraction) vs NDVI; correlation with LST
Key findings (with numbers): LST negatively correlated with vegetation abundance; vegetation fraction a better indicator than NDVI
Gap it suggests for my study: NDVI is an imperfect vegetation measure -> consider fraction-based or land-cover measures; scale matters

Citation: Brown, C.F., Brumby, S.P., Guzder-Williams, B. et al. Dynamic World, near real-time global 10 m land use land cover mapping. Scientific Data 9, 251
Key findings (with numbers): 9 classes incl. separate built, bare, trees, grass, crops, water; available in Earth Engine (GOOGLE/DYNAMICWORLD/V1); CC-BY 4.0
Limitations: Classification errors possible; must validate locally
Gap it suggests for my study: Solves two design problems: bare vs built (NDBI confusion) and trees vs grass (NDVI limitation)
